drafted_from: tool:keep-package-files-current's own row (its words, input schema, wake and steps) and the procedure in its README; read it before relying on it
start_here: Nothing to say: the engine runs tool:keep-package-files-current every 5 minutes on the Mac that holds the shared Workshop checkout. To read its last pass, say to your AI: "Show the last pass that kept the Workshop's package-files current." It answers the outcome (nothing-to-do, landed, origin-moved or error), the entries added and the findings (items the generator does not find, which origin keeps).
no_lists_because: It keeps no row: it adds to package-files.json on origin/main and returns what it found; nothing else is stored.
instructions: 1. Leave it on: the wake every-five-minutes runs the tool at the Mac that holds the shared Workshop checkout, with that checkout as its granted use-git-in-a-folder folder.

2. Read each pass: landed means one commit was added to origin/main with the entries the generator found that origin lacks; nothing-to-do means nothing was missing; origin-moved means origin changed during the pass and the next pass starts again; error means nothing was pushed and why says what held it.
3. Read the findings: each is an item or row origin has that the generator does not find. Origin keeps it, so it is never removed by this tool; its owner decides what to change, by hand.

worked_examples.title: Read the last pass
worked_examples.ask: Show the last pass that kept the Workshop's package-files current.
worked_examples.given: An empty input: the tool reads its granted checkout, not the input.
worked_examples.hands_back: A JSON pass result such as {"outcome":"nothing-to-do","at":"<origin commit>","added":0,"findings":[{"row":"tool:example","item":{"package":"example","paths":["do-work"],"at":"/opt/example"},"why":"the generator does not find this item; origin keeps it"}]}, where every finding names its row and why.
